prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The following table is a summary of the allocation of the allowance for credit losses at the end of the periods shown below:

The allowance for credit losses was $24.4 million, or 1.45% of loans outstanding, at September 30, 2026, compared to $21.1 million, or 1.42% of loans outstanding, at December 31, 2025. The ratio of the allowance for credit losses to non-performing loans was 248.71% at September 30, 2026, compared to 307.52% at December 31, 2025. The increase is mainly attributed to the PSL and PCD allowance added due to the FSC acquisition.

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table shows the principal components of non-interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

(1) Efficiency ratio is calculated as non-interest expense as a percent of revenue. Total revenue is calculated as net interest income plus non-interest income.

(2) Represents a non-GAAP financial measure. See the "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" section for a reconciliation of these measures.

Total non-interest expense increased $2.1 million, or 16.6%, to $14.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and increased $4.1 million, or 10.9%, to $41.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $37.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Salaries increased $0.01 million, or 0.2%, to $5.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and increased $0.8 million, or 4.7%, to $17.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $16.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

nonop.text:
The following table shows the principal components of non-interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

(1) Efficiency ratio is calculated as non-interest expense as a percent of revenue. Total revenue is calculated as net interest income plus non-interest income.

(2) Represents a non-GAAP financial measure. See the "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" section for a reconciliation of these measures.

Total non-interest expense increased $2.1 million, or 16.6%, to $14.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and increased $4.1 million, or 10.9%, to $41.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $37.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Salaries increased $0.01 million, or 0.2%, to $5.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and increased $0.8 million, or 4.7%, to $17.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $16.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income taxes as a percentage of earnings before income taxes as reported in the consolidated financial statements was 10.0% and 15.8% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 18.1% and 18.3% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The effective tax rate for each of the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was lower than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% primarily due to tax-free revenues, as well as the utilization of federal income tax credits purchased at a discount, which reduced tax expense during the current quarter.

net.text: Consolidated net income was $7.1 million, or $1.01 per diluted share, and $20.1 million, or $2.90 per diluted share, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $6.1 million, or $0.88 per diluted share, and $17.6 million, or $2.53 per diluted share, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Adjusted consolidated net income (1) was $8.6 million, or $1.23 per diluted share, and $22.2 million, or $3.20 per diluted share, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $6.1 million, or $0.88 per diluted share, and $17.6 million, or $2.53 per diluted share, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the return on average assets was 1.48% and 1.46%, respectively, the return on average stockholders’ equity was 14.91% and 14.80%, respectively, and the efficiency ratio was 65.00% and 63.33%, respectively. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the adjusted return on average assets (1) was 1.80% and 1.61%, respectively, the adjusted return on average stockholders’ equity (1) was 18.17% and 16.33%, respectively, and the adjusted efficiency ratio (1) was 55.64% and 59.04%, respectively.

Net interest income.text: The Company's primary source of revenue is net interest income derived primarily from lending and deposit taking activities. Much of the Company's business is commercial, commercial real estate development, and residential mortgage lending. The Company's income from mortgage brokerage activities is directly dependent on mortgage rates and the level of home purchases and refinancing activity.

intro.text: Hawthorn Bancshares, Inc., a bank holding company headquartered in Jefferson City, Missouri, is the parent company of Hawthorn Bank, which has served families and businesses for more than 160 years. Hawthorn Bank has multiple locations, including in the greater Kansas City metropolitan area, Jefferson City, Columbia, Springfield, and Clinton .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
